items.title: Growing a Neural Network in Breadth, Depth, and Time
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Eivinas Butkus, Kedar Garz\'on Gupta, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte
items.summary: arXiv:2605.25174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Brains and AI systems alike must achieve their goals with limited space, time, energy, and data. Here we focus on space and time, defining differentiable costs for breadth (channels), depth (layers), and time (recurrent steps) in a recurrent convolutional network. We optimize these costs jointly with task error via backpropagation. Pricing each resource differently, we grow a diverse set of computational graphs through optimization. We find that breadth, depth, and time can be traded off against each other at a given level of accuracy. Networks grow with task complexity and, when allowed to adaptively allocate time per input, take more recurrent steps if inputs are occluded. The time the model spends on each image also correlates with human reaction times, despite no training on human data. Our work takes a step toward a normative account of how spatial and temporal resource costs jointly shape neural architectures in brains and machines.

items.title: Persistence of Multifractal Dynamics at the Mammalian Neuromuscular Junction Across Extracellular Calcium Conditions
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Adriano J. da Silva, Sergio Floquet, Ricardo F. Lima
items.summary: arXiv:2611.25139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The neuromuscular junction represents a relevant experimental model for revealing important biophysical mechanisms underlying synaptic transmission. In this work, we revisited the time-series analysis of electrophysiological recordings obtained from mammalian diaphragm neuromuscular junctions. We applied multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) to assess whether intervals between spontaneous potentials exhibit multifractal behavior at physiological extracellular calcium concentrations and at hypocalcemic and hypercalcemic levels. Surprisingly, we observed a robust, stable multifractal profile across all electrophysiological recordings, regardless of calcium concentration. Therefore, our results provide support for a rich and complex scenario governing neurotransmitter release. Based on these findings, we discuss their biophysical significance and physiological implications.

items.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yanzhe Zhao, Yongzhang Ji
items.summary: arXiv:2610.25898v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns in continuous recordings. Repeated template reconstruction and time-pair correlation scans make analyses across brain regions, large cohorts, and parameter sweeps computationally prohibitive. We present HP-GSBS, an open-source implementation built on an exact mathematical reformulation that decomposes the matching objective into additive interval contributions from temporal prefix sums and computes Welch t-distance through constant-time rectangle queries over two-dimensional correlation prefix tables. Combined with streaming candidate search, local-window refinement, and active-block caching, this formulation drives unified CPU, PyTorch CUDA, and Triton backends. Across controlled benchmarks spanning recording lengths, feature dimensions, and search depths, HP-GSBS achieves 154- to 1,730-fold speedups while identically reproducing reference boundary histories and selected state counts (maximum $|\Delta\mathrm{TD}|=1.88\times10^{-11}$). Cross-backend numerical equivalence is further confirmed on four human electroencephalography recordings from the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset (120--173 states). Applied to naturalistic movie-viewing functional magnetic resonance imaging from 16 participants (4,230 angular-gyrus voxels), HP-GSBS completes group and individual fits in 213.10 s on a single CPU and reveals intersubject boundary alignment above a circular-shift null (mean pairwise $F_1=0.414$ vs. 0.325, $p=0.001$). HP-GSBS reduces hour-scale benchmark fits to seconds or fractions of a second. Recording-level parallelism and an optional low-memory execution path make cohort-level and multi-timescale analyses tractable on standard laboratory hardware.

items.title: Serial Dependence Emerges from Optimizing Vision for Noise Robustness
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Hiroshi Higashi, Keigo Sugihara, Yuichi Tanaka
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human visual perception is dynamically shaped by the recent past, a phenomenon known as serial dependence. Mechanistic models show that a residual memory trace can generate this dependency, yet its functional purpose (why the visual system should carry information forward in time at all) remains debated. We tested the hypothesis that serial dependence emerges as a normative consequence of optimizing vision for robustness against sensory noise. We trained recurrent autoencoders (a CNN encoder, a ConvGRU memory module, and a CNN decoder) to reconstruct natural videos corrupted by Gaussian noise, with no objective referring to perceptual history. Models that used their temporal memory achieved lower reconstruction error than memory-free counterparts, and this advantage widened as training noise increased, indicating that integrating past context is an adaptive denoising strategy. Probing the trained models with Gabor and dot sequences, we found that memory gave rise to serial dependence spontaneously: an attractive bias toward previous orientations and a spatial "continuity field" toward recently seen locations, both strengthening with training noise. Across temporal delays, the model's serial dependence was strongest for the immediately preceding stimulus and decayed monotonically. This profile quantitatively matched human orientation judgments, including an independent public dataset, once a known response-autocorrelation confound was controlled: an apparent non-monotonicity in one dataset reflected this measurement artifact rather than a genuine model-human mismatch. These findings suggest that serial dependence need not be an idiosyncratic quirk but can arise as a byproduct of optimizing for noise robustness, offering a normative account of perceptual history-dependence that complements existing mechanistic explanations and links behavior to an underlying computational objective.

items.title: Classical visual illusions in vision-language models under an instruction ladder
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Eiji Watanabe
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often name the "illusory" answer when shown a classical visual illusion, but it is unclear whether that answer comes from the picture or from knowledge about famous figures. We drew 300 new stimuli of 25 classical illusions in three conditions--the illusion, the illusion with its inducing elements reversed, and a control with the inducing elements removed--and asked about each image at eight rungs of an instruction ladder that runs from a false fact, through a neutral question and an instruction to report the physical truth, to telling the model the name of the illusion and finally the true answer. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, with thinking off and on, gave 460,800 answers. When asked for the physical fact, all four settings almost never gave the illusion answer, and they resolved real 10% differences in the same displays. When asked how the picture looks, the illusion answers returned, and they did not vanish after the true answer was stated. Two measures that cancel position preferences and recognition of the figure suggest that much of this depends on the stimulus: among side answers, Sonnet with thinking chose the illusion side in 85% of cases after being told the truth (95% CI 74--96%), with 16 of the 25 illusions showing a stimulus-driven effect. Yet for five figures--the Fraser spiral, Kanizsa triangle, Pinna--Brelstaff rings, Ouchi pattern and, for Haiku, the rotating snakes--the models gave the illusion answer to the control images as well, which suggests that they answered from the figure rather than from the effect. A false fact was mostly followed on control images but not on illusion images. The stimuli, prompts, all responses and the code are released for testing further models; the Python code that draws the stimuli is parametric and can generate new illusion images for other studies with models or human observers.

items.title: The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Sundeep Kapila
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Everyday stress is largely a learned pattern: a familiar cue, a fast reading of threat, an automatic reaction and a body that stays activated. Body-based practices such as mindfulness, interoceptive training, Somatic Experiencing and yoga target these patterns, but they are usually taught as techniques without a map of the mechanism they act on. Pain neuroscience education suggests that understanding such a mechanism can itself change experience. No comparable model exists for everyday self-regulation. This paper proposes the Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback, developed over six cohorts of a workshop for non-clinical adults. The loop describes any action as four steps: Sense (exteroception, proprioception and interoception), Process (perception as inference, weighted by context and safety), Choose (habitual reaction or goal-directed response after a pause) and Execute (autonomic and somatic output). Feedback from each outcome acts beneath all four steps, through synaptic plasticity, habit formation and allostatic load. The paper integrates the perception-action cycle, information-processing stages of choice, interoceptive inference, the autonomic space model and the defence cascade. It places a set of practices on the loop: full sensory awareness, grounding, orientation, resourcing, the pause, reduced stimulus and choice, slow movement and relaxation, each with a proposed mechanism and an assessment of the evidence. It also describes the model's translation into four practitioner skills. Seven testable propositions are derived for future evaluation. The model is offered as a teachable framework for wellbeing, not a treatment.

items.title: Self-organized fractional silencing of pyramidal neurons under global depolarization in a spatial neuron-glial microcircuit model
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Stanislav V. Lagosha, Andrey Yu. Verisokin, Darya V. Verveyko, Alyona V. Berezhnaya, Nadezda A. Brazhe, Alexey R. Brazhe
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pathological transitions in nervous tissue, including epileptiform discharges and cortical spreading depolarization, depend on the interplay between cellular and interstitial mechanisms. We develop a biophysically detailed two-dimensional model of the neurogliovascular unit (NGVU) integrating neuronal populations in the Hodgkin-Huxley formalism, astrocyte-regulated extracellular potassium dynamics, extracellular neurotransmitter spillover, and noradrenergic neuromodulation. Numerical simulations show that inhibitory interneurons enter depolarization block (DB) at significantly lower extracellular potassium concentrations and stimulation intensities than pyramidal neurons. Early loss of inhibition shifts the local excitation-inhibition balance and triggers network hyperexcitability. In the spatially extended network, exceeding a critical stimulation threshold induces a transition from heterogeneous but spatially uniform firing to network fragmentation into stable active microclusters with self-sustained high-frequency firing. Pyramidal neurons with lower excitatory synaptic input receive less recurrent excitation, which protects them from DB. By continuously releasing potassium ions and glutamate into the extracellular space, pyramidal neurons drive strong depolarization in more densely connected neighbors and push them into deep DB. Simulations of localized astrocytic dysfunction predict a spatial limit for potassium clearance defects. Small damaged cores are fully compensated by diffusion and uptake by surrounding healthy astrocyte units. However, above a critical damage size, activity-dependent potassium buildup and firing positive feedback disrupt homeostasis in surrounding units, promoting persistent depolarized centers with self-sustained, spatially segregated pathological activity.

items.title: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Darya V. Verveyko, Andrey Yu. Verisokin, Pavel O. Lukin
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arachidonic acid metabolites can have both vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects, thereby influencing neuronal activity. In this work, to analyze possible patterns of activity of nervous tissue in response to changes in the metabolic profile, a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of connected neurogliovascular units was developed. We simulate the influence of arachidonic acid metabolites on the dynamics of the neurogliovascular unit during cortical spreading depression in order to determine the ways in which astrocytic activity influences the spatiotemporal characteristics of the propagating cortical depression wave. It is assumed that in the future the results of the theoretical study can be used to find ways to remove nervous tissue from pathological conditions that occur in epilepsy, migraines and a number of neurodegenerative diseases, including those associated with the occurrence of cortical depression waves.

items.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Mirko Morello, Shivang Rawat, David J. Heeger
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Each RQF acts as a band-pass filter whose selectivity is determined by two learnable parameters: its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity. In the windowed mode, the summary of the current window predicts the summary of a later window; in the dense mode, the state at the current timestep predicts future log-power. Each RQF encoder is pretrained on a dataset and then a readout (e.g., a task-specific classifier) is trained on the output of the RQF encoder, with the encoder either frozen or fully fine-tuned. For multichannel EEG and intracranial recordings, a shared encoder processes each channel separately, and a spatial readout combines the channel representations using electrode locations. Across four neural benchmarks using scalp or intracranial EEG, the pretrained RQF system performs close to the state of the art while using a small fraction of the parameters of the competing models. For example, a 110k-parameter RQF system achieves 0.9247 +/- 0.0022 test AUROC on 100-s TUAB segments, above SAMBA (0.9054) at the same context with 9 times as many parameters, and 0.9040 +/- 0.0019 on 10-s segments, comparable to EEG foundation models with 3.2M-369M parameters.

items.title: From Novel Combinations to Informative Absence: Structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice in language learning
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yanzhe Zhao
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language learners must infer which novel expressions are grammatically licensed and when continued absence is evidence against them. Our generative theory unites these capacities via counterfactual expression opportunities, decomposing utterance generation into structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice. First, shared predictive continuations recover structural permission for unseen word-construction pairings across 30 artificial grammars (mean AUC 0.945 after 120 sentences). Second, under hierarchical uncertainty, we derive a joint evidence law linking omissions to context diversity and within-context repetition, and an exact finite-sample context-refinement inequality. Thus, observing related expressions calibrates expected use to sharpen negative evidence, and higher expected use can drive steeper posterior declines for stronger-permission candidates (reversing initial order after six omissions in a fixed-rate example). Third, we prove that while raw counts confound semantic availability and form selection, scene-level opportunity observations identify both. Empirically, reanalyzing adult and child artificial-language experiments shows meaning-conditioned restriction; judgments of restricted combinations improve held-out production predictions across 399 participants (+0.036 nats/production). Naturalistic child-directed and child speech (11 families, six corpora) shows pervasive source-level usage clustering beyond lexical, number, and dependency-role controls, grounding hierarchical rate uncertainty. Finally, modeling causative judgments across five languages shows that structural compatibility and calibrated usage probabilities draw on distinct distributional, semantic, and discriminative cues. Together, these findings show how the organization and calibration of communicative opportunities govern the evidential value of linguistic absence.

items.title: Direction and speed selectivity properties for spatio-temporal receptive fields according to the generalized Gaussian derivative model for visual receptive fields
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Tony Lindeberg
items.summary: arXiv:2511.08101v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper gives an in-depth theoretical analysis of the direction and speed selectivity properties of idealized models of the spatio-temporal receptive fields of simple cells and complex cells, based on the generalized Gaussian derivative model for visual receptive fields. According to this theory, the receptive fields are modelled as velocity-adapted affine Gaussian derivatives for different image velocities and different degrees of elongation. By probing such idealized receptive field models of visual neurons to moving sine waves with different angular frequencies and image velocities, we characterize the computational models to a structurally similar probing method as is used for characterizing the direction and speed selective properties of biological neurons. By comparison to results of neurophysiological measurements of direction and speed selectivity for biological neurons in the primary visual cortex, we find that our theoretical results are consistent with (i) velocity-tuned visual neurons that are sensitive to particular motion directions and speeds, and (ii) different visual neurons having broader vs. sharper direction and speed selective properties. Our theoretical results in combination with results from neurophysiological characterizations of motion-sensitive visual neurons are also consistent with a previously formulated hypothesis that the simple cells in the primary visual cortex ought to be covariant under local Galilean transformations, so as to enable processing of visual stimuli with different motion directions and speeds.

items.title: Causal Event Networks: Entangled Tensor Graphs, Connectome Quotient Topology, and Subjective Experience as Geometric Dual
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Vahid R. Ramezani
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a chromatically constrained tensor-product construction that generates sparse recurrent computational graphs whose coloring bounds the number of sequential execution phases: vertices are computational units, edges are causal message-passing channels, and the graph can grow arbitrarily large while its chromatic causal depth stays fixed. Coarsened to the scale of the Budapest Reference Connectome, the community quotient of a simple local construction reproduces the connectome's broad degree profile, passes a nine-criterion topological test and comes close to the connectome on most of a further battery of complexity, spectral, controllability and clique measures, while the fine parent graph shows a scale separation: multiscale organization is intrinsic to the fine graph, and short-path integration appears only under coarsening. Placing short-path integration directly in the fine substrate, with chromatically admissible bridges and targeted sparsification, yields quotients far less modular than the connectome across a wide range of coarsening schemes. items.title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Prapti Roy, Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. Brain region names, numeric formatting, and prompt framing shift what a model predicts without improving how well it separates ADHD subjects from Controls; perturbing the graph changes predictions no more for clinically meaningful regions than for random ones; and the models' own justifications contradict the values they cite, inconsistently interpreting the connectivity evidence provided to them. Across every probe, predictions follow the model's built-in class bias and the surface form of the prompt rather than the subject's connectivity, calling into question a premise underlying current LLM brain integration work. Our code is available at https://github.com/Roy025/ADHD-code.

items.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Sylvain Carrozza, Johann Chevrier, Luca Lionni
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

items.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Chia-Ho Ou
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

items.title: Single-realization Pauli twirling for suppressing coherent error accumulation in structured quantum circuits
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Dihang Sun, Tianqi Chen, Jin Ming Koh, Nannan Ma, Jiangbin Gong
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pauli twirling is conventionally understood as an ensemble-level noise-tailoring procedure which suppresses coherent components of the error channel by averaging over randomized compilations. This picture does not by itself determine whether a single realization of Pauli-dressed circuit can outperform its bare counterpart, nor does it predict when such an advantage should occur. In this work, we present single-realization based framework for the standard Pauli dressing of two-qubit Clifford gates in structured quantum circuits. This is afforded by the key insight that for weak coherent errors, the leading gate infidelity is governed by the variance of some accumulated error generator. Through both simulations and theoretical considerations, we verify that coherent errors accumulated at different entangling gates can produce $\Theta(L^2)$ variance growth in a bare circuit, whereas independent Pauli dressing eliminates the cross-layer contribution on average and yields an $O(L)$ variance bound at any fixed confidence level for a single randomly sampled realization. We then develop a covariance diagnostic that predicts when this mechanism is effective in error mitigation. We find a strong Pauli twirling advantage for coherent errors whose transported generators have large off-diagonal covariance, and little advantage when the covariance matrix is nearly diagonal. Hardware experiments on IBM superconducting processors demonstrate fidelity improvements for GHZ-state preparation and reduced observable errors in Trotterized transverse-field Ising dynamics. These results indicate that single realizations of Pauli twirling without ensemble averaging is a useful coherent-error suppression technique for structured circuits containing repeated nontrivial two-qubit operations.

items.title: Beyond the Stabilizer Norm: Physicality and Resource Allocation in Pauli-Limited Quantum Certification
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Shreya Savadatti, Peter Yun Zhang
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Certification from restricted and uncertain Pauli measurements can be posed as a robust optimization problem: among all physical channels consistent with the data, how small can the fidelity with a target channel be? We first study a linear relaxation that ignores positivity and show that it is exactly characterized by a single scalar, the stabilizer norm of the target Choi state, $s_{\mathrm{wit}}(U)=\|C_U\|_{\mathrm{st}}-1/D$. We then ask whether this scalar continues to determine robustness once the positivity constraint is restored. It does not. We derive a necessary and sufficient KKT condition for the relaxation to remain tight, together with a dual obstruction certifying a strict gap, and give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that two distinct two-qubit targets can have exactly the same stabilizer norm but different physical robustness. The KKT condition depends on structure discarded by the stabilizer norm, including the support and relative signs of the Choi-Pauli coefficients and the algebraic relations among the corresponding Pauli operators. We use this structure to derive simpler sufficient certificates for a strict gap. The dual coefficients also determine how measurement uncertainty enters the finite-data fidelity bound. For a fixed budget, we derive exact shot-allocation rules for a fixed certificate and for compatible observables obtained from shared measurement settings, and we formulate the corresponding joint certificate-design problem. The conjecture that every full-support two-qubit target has positive gain remains open.

items.title: Communication advantages of a quantum switch of two pure-loss channels
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Carlo Marconi
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum switch can enable communication through otherwise unusable channels, a phenomenon known as causal activation. We show that a switch of two identical pure-loss channels can achieve strictly greater energy-constrained classical and quantum capacities than their sequential use, even when two-way classical communication is available. Remarkably, the switch also activates quantum communication over a range of transmissivities for which the sequential channel has zero quantum capacity.

items.title: Block Search Conditioned on Features for Sequential Quantum Data Encoding
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Cec\'ilia S. C. Botelho, Erico S. Teixeira, Anderson F. P. dos Santos, Guilherme D. Lima, Helida Santos, Adenauer Yamin, Renata Reiser, In\^es de Castro Dutra
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential quantum data encoding is addressed through the joint selection of input features and encoding blocks within a fixed quantum register. At each step, a new feature, a block of operations, its placement, and its rotation weights are selected together from training data, extending the incremental construction of Q-FLAIR. With direct-loss selection (RAW), nine to twelve features were retained in four qubits across five new Bars and Stripes datasets. Under the same final calibration, mean changes relative to the calibrated Q-FLAIR reference were +5.53 percentage points in balanced accuracy, -15.83% in binary cross-entropy (BCE), and +7.79% in area under the ROC curve (AUC). The prespecified success criterion was met in four of five datasets and for the mean paired differences. These results were obtained by comparing complete procedures under a common cap of 32 operations.

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Kun Zhou, Meng Cao
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper aims to uncover new phenomena and provide new tools for quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. The initial motivation is to identify the main reason for the existence of impure cases in such quantum codes. Our main result reveals that whether \(d = r+1\) is the key factor governing the impurity of quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. We prove that, when \(d \neq r+1\), impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs have bounded lengths. Conversely, when \(d = r+1\), we construct impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs with unbounded lengths. The central tool developed in this work is a criterion for identifying impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. The main results include a criterion for impurity in quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorem 3.2), a construction framework for impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorem 4.4), and two families of impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorems 4.8 and 4.11).

items.title: Quantum control of an electrically levitated nanoparticle with a trapped ion
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Bernard Faulend, Dmitry S. Bykov, Tracy E. Northup, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum control of levitated nanoparticles offers a route towards macroscopic quantum states. Here we propose a novel way to achieve it for a nanoparticle levitated electrically in a linear Paul trap together with a single ion, a system recently realized experimentally. By suitably engineering the trap's AC potential, one can parametrically modulate the ion-nanoparticle distance and thus the Coulomb coupling to enable a resonant interaction. For realistic parameters, we calculate that this enables sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle to its motional ground state by a single, continuously laser-cooled ion. Additional AC drives enable the preparation of squeezed nanoparticle states and of ion-nanoparticle entanglement. Moreover, non-Gaussian states such as Fock and cat states, prepared in the ion with standard trapped-ion techniques, can be transferred to the nanoparticle with high fidelities. We provide complete protocols for each of these states, including all known decoherence sources. Our results establish electrically trapped ion-nanoparticle systems as a platform for quantum control of levitated matter.

items.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: P\'{e}ter Naszvadi, Marcell Tukora, Roman Ku\v{z}el, M\'{a}ty\'{a}s Koniorczyk
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yunqi Huang, Wei Zi, Jianhao He, Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct exact circuits for $n$-qubit Dicke states of any Hamming weight $k$ using $O(n)$ single-qubit gates and CNOTs in $O(\log n)$ depth without ancillary qubits. The gate count and depth are asymptotically optimal for every $0<k<n$. We compress symmetric blocks to free output qubits for weight-dependent phases. A sign correction followed by a collective rotation produces a state whose overlap with the target is at least a positive constant, so exact amplitude amplification takes $O(1)$ steps. For balanced Dicke states ($k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$), the logarithmic depth disproves the $\Omega(k)$ depth lower bound conjectured by Yuan and Zhang (2025).

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Hongchao Li, Marius Lemm
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent $\alpha\in(D,D+1)$ in $D$ spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with $\alpha\in (1,3/2)$, whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.

items.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Fernando Mondragon-Sampedro, Diego Alvarez-Estevez
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though this protective effect diminishes in highly expressive structural settings.

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: F. S. Luiz, D Abreu, A. J. G. Abel\'em, J. E. Da Fonseca, A. F. P. Santos, M. C. de Oliveira
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-optimization benchmarks can show reduced energy while concealing local loss of weighted covariance. We combine encoding checks with exact structural references to select informative circuit diagnostics for static geographic coverage instances. The executed 24-qubit surrogate has infeasible ground states, whereas a faithful 51-qubit slack encoding preserves its 13 support-graph components and remains exactly simulable blockwise. At the executed angles, the total ideal optimum probability is $5.47\times10^{-20}$, making optimum counts uninformative at the executed budget of $10^5$ shots. A product distribution with the measured bit marginals accounts for about $90\%$ of the observed energy reduction. In three fixed-circuit jobs, the global weighted-covariance ratio is approximately $0.50$, while a five-variable block has ratios between $0.12$ and $0.28$ and contributes only $3.7\%$ of the ideal global denominator. Simultaneous bands resolve its deficit relative to the global ratio under an exploratory conditional counting model. The exact block reference thus reveals a local discrepancy concealed by the aggregate, without identifying an error mechanism or establishing device stability. The procedure links benchmark structure to the resolution and limitations of its observables.

items.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: G. C. Borges, M. Duclerc, G. Palacios, A. A. C. de Almeida, N. R. de Melo, D. Felinto
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. The measured Cauchy-Schwarz parameter exceeds unity in both configurations, with a higher central value with filtering ($\overline{R} = 4.15 \pm 0.93$) than without ($\overline{R} = 2.33 \pm 0.20$). This architecture provides actively stabilized rejection of a narrow spectral interval, simultaneously, for two fields detected in different directions. Filter performance could be further improved by adjusting the cavity linewidth to better match the spectral width of the central component and by reducing losses in the filters.

items.title: geodesiq: a Python package for geometric diabatic-adiabatic optimal state transfer
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: David Fern\'andez-Fern\'andez, Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Gloria Platero
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the geodesiq Python package, which implements a geometric framework for shaping control pulses that achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems. The underlying method combines adiabatic and diabatic control into a single metric, suppressing unwanted excitations while allowing selected diabatic passages. Finding the pulse thereby reduces to solving a single first-order ordinary differential equation. We explain how to use geodesiq and illustrate its use explicitly with Landau-Zener transitions, spin-qubit initialization, adiabatic many-body ground-state preparation, and a diabatic-adiabatic transfer in a four-level system.

items.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Weijie Du, Filippo Fornetti, James P. Vary
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.

items.title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Pouriya Ghadimi, Maximilian Fr\"ohlich, Aaron Sander, Martin Eigel, Richard M. Milbradt
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schr\"odinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

items.title: Explicit construction of the normal cone at every nonlocal extreme behaviour of $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$ and device-independent applications
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yutian Wu, Xie Sicheng, Ravishankar Ramanathan
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The set of quantum correlations $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$, in the simplest Bell scenario with two parties performing two binary measurements each, is an object of fundamental interest both in quantum foundations and for device-independent applications. A nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this set can maximize many different Bell expressions, yet these expressions are not all equally useful in a practical experiment. Here, firstly, we give an explicit characterization of every Bell expression maximized by any given nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this Bell scenario. This determines the full normal cone at every such behaviour and makes it possible to optimize over all Bell tests with the same ideal behavior. We then derive an exact variational formula for the quantum bound of an arbitrary Bell expression in this scenario. As an example illustrating the construction, we derive the normal cone for a family of extremal quantum behaviours of importance in device-independent randomness certification, from Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 150403, 2022. Finally, we explore the consequences of this characterization for device-independent randomness generation in practical experiments. Specifically, for any given detection efficiency $\eta \in [0.75,0.98]$, we construct Bell tests and two-qubit experiments that certify more single-round min-entropy from one Bell score than any CHSH score can certify with the same detector efficiency, even when the quantum devices used for the CHSH test are optimized. The results provide a systematic way to choose Bell tests for a desired quantum behaviour and to improve their performance for device-independent applications under experimental imperfections.

items.title: The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J. -Q. Liang
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbar\omega(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form $\pm i\hbar\omega(z(d/dz)+1/2)$, and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. The two convergence domains correspond to one-sided contraction semigroups of dilations. Finally, we construct bi-coherent states whose biorthogonal position and momentum second cumulants are purely imaginary and complex conjugate, with product $\hbar^2/4$. The corresponding Heisenberg expectation values follow the exact classical hyperbolic trajectories for arbitrary real initial positions and momenta.

items.title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Tianchun Zhou
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

items.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Sayantan Ganguly
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

items.title: Trotter Error Bounds in Lean 4 with a Cancellation-Aware Analysis of the Fourth-Order Suzuki Formula
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Bingyu Xia, Jue Xu, Yue Wang
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize the commutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. in Lean 4. For skew-adjoint generators, the local order condition gives an explicit integer step count sufficient to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We apply the theorem in Lean to the binary fourth-order Suzuki formula. For this formula we can also account for cancellation within and between steps. Using local remainder estimates of Casas and Murua, we sum the signed quintic and centered seventh-degree error terms after conjugating each to the interaction picture. For every positive integer step count, we bound the difference between this sum and the global error operator. At fixed time the explicit remainder is eighth order in the step size, and the integral of the conjugated quintic term gives the exact leading error coefficient. The Lean proofs cover the two-generator finite-sum estimates, including the spectral norm for complex matrices. On five ten-site nearest-neighbor Heisenberg instances at time $10$ and tolerance $10^{-3}$, the transported sum meets the tolerance at a mean of $129.4$ steps. Taking a separate norm at each step with the same polynomial and remainder gives a mean first crossing between $184.6$ and $185.2$ steps. The accumulated Casas--Murua local bound at $q=8$ gives a mean of $184.8$ steps.

items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Leonardo Gaytan, Bradley Lloyd, Paul Kliewer, Chandler Wilburn, Lincoln D. Carr, Adam McCaughan, Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.

items.title: Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Ai Zhang, Yan-Zhe Song, Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of $\kappa_B = 2\kappa_A$, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.

items.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. items.title: Pulse-tube-vibration induced Larmor frequency jitter in anisotropic Kramers spins
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: R. Shaik, P. Kesarwani, S. Rajendran, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of pulse-tube mechanical vibrations towards spin frequency noise in a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator. Our system comprises of a low mode-volume superconducting resonator coupled to 50 ppm $\text{Er}^{3+}:\text{CaWO}_4$ spins with highly anisotropic g-factors. By measuring single-shot spin echoes using narrow-bandwidth three-pulse sequences, we directly observe a vibration induced stochastic signal resulting from the spin's Larmor frequency moving into and out of the detection bandwidth. We also benchmark the system as a quantum sensor for angular fluctuations, extracting a noise floor of 350 nanodegrees.

items.title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jerry Horgan, Indrakshi Dey, Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

items.title: Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: V\'ictor M. Villalba
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, $U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a)$, for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-P\'erot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schr\"odinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition $\delta(\kappa)+\kappa d=n\pi$, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase $\delta$. We also calculate the post-selection probability $P_{RT}$, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.

items.title: Augmenting Quantum Neural Networks with Contractive Layers
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical neural networks combine diverse layers with complementary roles to achieve rich expressive capabilities across complex learning tasks. Rapid advances in quantum science and technology have motivated growing interest in their quantum counterparts, quantum neural networks, raising the question of how their expressivity can be enhanced through the design of new quantum layers. Of particular interest are layers that enrich the accessible function space while introducing only a small number of additional trainable parameters. In this Letter, we introduce the contractive layer as a promising building block for quantum neural networks. This layer comprises all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter, enabling efficient control of quantum information flow while maintaining experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays. Using observable learning as a benchmark, we show that contractive layers enhance expressivity more efficiently than simply increasing the depth of conventional brick-wall circuits. This advantage stems from a systematic increase in the accessible target-space dimension per trainable parameter. We further demonstrate similar improvements in image recognition tasks. These results highlight contractive layers as a practical route to expressive quantum neural networks on near-term quantum devices.

items.title: Generalized Wigner-Yanase Uncertainty Bounds for Multiple Quantum Channels
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing
items.summary: arXiv:2611.27034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive uncertainty relations for quantum channels based on the generalized Wigner-Yanase skew information. For three channels, we obtain a product lower bound by optimizing over permutations of commutator and anticommutator pairings. For an arbitrary number of channels, we establish a lower bound on the sum of squared uncertainties and construct a hierarchy of bounds using the partial Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. These bounds are invariant under changes of Kraus representation for a fixed operator basis. The first two levels of the hierarchy coincide with the elementary arithmetic-geometric mean bound, while the intermediate levels generally depend on the ordering of the operator basis. Examples involving three and four qubit channels demonstrate the bounds and compare their performance with an earlier pairing inequality under fixed channel representations.

items.title: Frequency-bin-encoded quantum secret sharing with fast basis switching
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Chen-You Su, Suparna Seshadri, Hsuan-Hao Lu, Jason D. McKinney, Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-bin encoding offers unique opportunities for fiber-native quantum information processing, yet its full potential has been hampered by challenges in rapid state control and protocol scaling. Leveraging high-speed microwave processing, we overcome several extant hurdles and unlock new fundamental capabilities in frequency-based quantum communications. First, we demonstrate three-party quantum secret sharing, representing, to our knowledge, the first multiparty ($N\geq 3$ users) quantum communication protocol implemented entirely with frequency encoding. Second, we demonstrate active, pseudorandom switching of frequency-bin quantum states and measurement bases at 20 MHz symbol rates, enabling real-time protocol operation without relying on hardware-intensive passive basis-selection schemes. Even under fast switching, we preserve high-contrast three-party correlations ($\geq 0.91$) and low quantum bit error rates ($\leq 4.5\%$). Our work extends frequency-bin quantum communication beyond static, two-party protocols, opening a pathway toward scalable, reconfigurable, and real-time spectrally encoded quantum networking.

items.title: Scheduling the quantum implementation of the Trotter decomposition for Hamiltonian simulation
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Augustin Ho (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, \'Ecole des Mines de Saint-\'Etienne), Naoki Yamamoto (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, Quantum Computing Center, Keio University)
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the quantum computational task for Hamiltonian simulation, the arrangement in which sub-Hamiltonians appear in the Trotter decomposition may have a large influence on the precision, under a given circuit complexity. In this paper, we design several scheduling strategies by combining two methods; that is, the existing simultaneous diagonalization scheme leveraged in order to guarantee the performance in a relatively short circuit depth, with a method inspired from a Trotter-Suzuki decomposition of the second or the fourth order for a better accuracy. By conducting numerical simulations on various Hamiltonian instances, we confirm a systematic advantage over previous methods. Thus, our proposal may eliminate the need of dealing with several Hamiltonian-dependent scheduling strategies.

items.title: Analog Explorations of Quantum State Measurement
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The awkward disconnect in the postulates of quantum mechanics between the continuous, deterministic, linear, and unitary evolution governed by Schr\"odinger's equation and the discontinuous, stochastic, nonlinear, and nonunitary measurement process has vexed physicists for decades. Intuition from classical mechanics, statistical mechanics, and dynamical systems theory suggests that such a process might be modeled with a nonlinear system of differential equations. We explore such approaches by designing a deterministic model of an ideal projective measurement on a single qubit and constructing an analog computer that simulates it by manipulating voltages in an electrical circuit. The model reduces to Schr\"odinger evolution when no measurement is taking place. During a measurement, a hidden variable that the observer does not resolve selects the outcome, and the model is constructed so that a uniformly distributed hidden variable yields Born-rule frequencies. We do not derive the Born rule; rather, we show that a deterministic dynamical system with no intrinsic noise can implement it. Over 300 trials, the circuit reproduces the ideal model's individual outcomes to within one percent of the decision threshold, and its outcome frequencies match the Born rule to within about 0.02 in probability. These results are a small but provocative step towards modeling quantum measurement with macro-scale machines---a step of interest for both the foundations of physics and the alternatives to digital computing it suggests.

items.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

items.title: Efficient Tensor Decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like Potentials and Its Application to Probing Molecular Geometries Using a Quantum Computer
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: James Brown, Masashi Takahashi, Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an efficient canonical polyadic decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like potentials in real-space grid representations suited to quantum computing applications. By decomposing the matrix elements of Coulomb-like potentials into low-rank Cartesian components, we achieve $O(N^{1/3})$ T-gate scaling per Coulomb term, where $N$ is the number of grid points (basis functions) per electron, while maintaining high accuracy. This opens a path to significantly reducing the number of basis functions (i.e., qubits) required compared to previous methods by utilizing improved representations of the Coulomb potential that converge faster with grid spacing. The decomposition is also valid for certain pseudopotentials, which can decrease the cost significantly compared to previous work. This efficient decomposition enables the application of block-encoding techniques at larger grid spacings than with previous decompositions, and can therefore be used for algorithms that do not require high energy accuracy. We apply this decomposed Coulomb potential to hydrogen atom energy levels, the helium ground-state energy, and the Hartree-Fock potential energy curve of LiH, and show that modest basis sizes achieve semi-quantitative to quantitative accuracy. As an example of where these faster-converging Coulomb representations can be used on a quantum computer, we discuss their application to probing low-energy molecular geometries, and we estimate the resulting reduction in the cost of real-time evolution.

items.title: Gravity-induced entanglement assisted by an additional interaction using magic angle calibration
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravity-induced entanglement provides an operational test of whether gravitational dynamics are compatible with local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but the weakness of the gravitational interaction and the presence of force noise make direct entanglement generation extremely demanding. We introduce a controllable additional coherent interaction that biases two test masses close to, but within, a separability-preservation bound, so that the weak Newtonian coupling supplies only the remaining coherent contribution needed for entanglement. If the additional interaction alone is shown to be incapable of generating entanglement, while entanglement is observed when gravity is included, the gravitational interaction provides a non-LOCC contribution. Since gravity cannot be turned off, we use a magic-angle null of the projected tidal coupling to calibrate the additional interaction and force noise. If the additional dynamics is certified to preserve separability at the magic angle and entanglement is subsequently observed in a non-null configuration, the gravitational contribution is incompatible with an LOCC description within the Markovian model. The protocol trades the stringent absolute force-noise requirement of direct schemes for precision in controlling the additional coupling, its backaction, and angle-dependent systematics.

items.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yicheng Song, Zhipeng Yang, Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka
items.summary: arXiv:2611.26762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.
